To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown a significant decrease of activated CD8+ GrB+ cytotoxic cells, a decrease in the CD4+ T cell count, and a decrease in the ratio of CD4+ to CD8+ T cells in HIV-associated Hodgkin lymphoma.
HIV-associated Hodgkin lymphoma is a distinct disease entity with unique biological features.

the inflammatory infiltrate of classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) in HIV-infected patients is composed of a decreased number of CD4+ cells and activated cytotoxic cells, and an increased number of nonactivated cytotoxic CD8 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the immune response to cHL in HIV-infected patients.

the role of cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) in the pathogenesis of HIV-associated Hodgkins disease (HIV-HL) and the role of CTL in the pathogenesis and prognosis of classical Hodgkin's disease in general.
the role of the immune response on the outcome of HIV-associated cHL and the impact of the HIV infection on the antitumor immunity in cHL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inflammatory infiltrate in cHL is different in HIV-infected patients compared to controls.
in cHL the immune system is not able to recognize and eliminate the malignant cells and that this is not related to the HIV infection but rather to the underlying disease.
the inflammatory background in HIV-associated c HL is characterized by a striking inversion in the ratio of CD4/CD 8 T lymphocytes and a significant decrease in the number of GrB+ cytotoxic T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-associated cHL is associated with a decrease in CD4+ T-cell infiltration and a decrease in GrB+ cytotoxic T cells, which could contribute to the poor prognosis of HIV-associated cHL.
HIV-infected individuals with cHL have a decreased CD4/CD4 ratio and a decrease in activated cytotoxic T cells.
HIV-infected patients with cHL have a higher frequency of MC histological subtypes and advanced disease stages, and a poor response to therapy, and a lower survival rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune response in HIV-associated cHl is different from the one in HIV-negative cHl.

the inflammatory background of cHL differs between HIV+ and HIV- patients, with a striking decrease in CD4+ T cell and cytotoxic T cells in HIV+ patients, which might have an impact on the immune response against the tumor cells.
the HIV infection has a strong impact on the inflammatory background of cHL.
